invariants: Manila (#D2B98C) owns more than 40% of the room's pixel area in the filed state — a finding that shrinks cards to accent-sized chips is rejected however much cleaner it looks. The cards are the page, the cabinet is the frame.

Aniline (#5C3D91) is a flat stamp-ink solid, never a gradient, never a brand wash — the gradient is the AI tell of 2026, not the hue. Any proposal introducing a violet gradient or accent wash is rejected on sight.
Onionskin (#E9E2D2) stays a component inside an opened drawer, never a page ground — promoting it to a page background lands the direction in the cream-and-serif default by the side door.
The stamp stays typographic: no distress textures, no rotation past 2.5 degrees — texture reads as a Photoshop filter, and decoration is what a skeptic dismisses.

Contrast is measured, not eyeballed — every CSS file carries a recorded table against a 4.5:1 floor for text and 3:1 for controls and visual boundaries. A finding that moves a colour pair must restate the measured ratio or it is not shippable.
Zero third-party requests at runtime — fonts and JS libraries are vendored under web/vendor/. No finding may introduce a CDN link or any hosted asset.
No build step — web/ is hand-written CSS and ES modules served straight off a StaticFiles mount. No framework, no Tailwind, no bundler proposals.

The prefers-reduced-motion override must stay AFTER the default in web/tokens.css — both rules target :root at equal specificity, so source order decides. Reordering silently defeats the accessibility feature; it already shipped broken once.
Copy never says "verified", never promises a duration, never flatters the user — institutional register, evidence-first. DIRECTION.md's "What the UI is now obliged to do" outranks any copy finding.

waves.name: runs-and-work
waves.rationale: The five findings where a user loses work, loses a credential, or keeps paying for a run they can no longer see. One blast radius across app.js, shell.js, scriptcheck.js, account.js and auth.js, and four of the five are small edits against machinery the app already ships.
waves.closeOut: ran 2026-08-11 pre-merge, in two passes. The first closed F-004, F-005 and F-013 and found a defect the wave introduced: setLiveRun(null) and clearStashedRun() were missing from the abandon path, so walking away from a run left the rail routing to an emptied progress panel for a run still spending. Fixed in resetProgress and guarded by a test that fails when either line is removed. A third build then closed F-001 and F-003, re-captured 06-progress-running, and verified the abandon path live. Seven comment-drift items fixed.

waves.name: without-sight-or-a-mouse
waves.rationale: The five findings that make the app usable without sight or a mouse. Chosen over the higher-ranked F-002 because that one still carries two unresolved design questions, and over the plugin's consistency-first default because those four render byte-identical pixels and make nothing downstream cheaper. This class is invisible in all 14 captures and undetectable by axe or Lighthouse, which is why it is still here.
waves.closeOut: ran 2026-08-11 pre-merge, six commits, all five closed. Five of the register's fix directions were wrong and are corrected in the wave ledger: F-006's scrollBehavior reuse is not buildable (focus() takes no behavior option) and its named heading did not exist; F-010's headline misses two failure surfaces in account.js and over-states why the banner was silent; F-009's "unrecorded" ratio was already recorded at shell.css:319. The close-out found a defect the wave introduced: appending the status word to .rail-room-meta wraps to a second line in a 300px rail at some era lengths, making a flagged row taller than its neighbours. A flagged row now replaces the era rather than appending to it. Also caught pre-commit: the result region shipped ANONYMOUS behind 18 passing source assertions, because Chromium computes no name for aria-labelledby pointing at a descendant — found only by reading the live accessibility tree.

waves.name: the-evidence-itself
waves.rationale: One finding, because it is the app's primary evidence surface and no lens filed it. Measured on the filed Gdansk room: 17 of 17 citation-rail excerpts and 10 of 12 drawer clips render raw scraped markdown as literal characters, uncapped, at a median of 1462 characters. The citation block is 82% of a card whose answer is 1.2% of it. F-002 was scoped alongside this and deliberately held back: its real fix is a star/verdicts.py contract change that would push unannotated claims into unverifiable, and that needs its own measurement rather than a decision made while building something else.

deferred.F-002: Held for wave 5. Its fix direction demotes VERDICT_READING to a slug, which would make the four of nine cards that carry no note worse rather than better. Blocked on whether confirmed and anachronism should require a note the way unverifiable already does.

waves.closeOut: ran 2026-08-11 pre-merge. F-025 closed in one commit, because the module, both wirings and both comment corrections are one behaviour change with one test. The format check the brief demanded first paid for itself: both renderers described an HTML payload with entities, and across all 104 stored excerpts 5 carry <strong>, none carry an entity, and the large majority are markdown. It also corrected the brief itself, which said to drop structural lines and join what was left — joining manufactures a passage the page never contained, so a structural line now ends a run instead. Close-out found two defects the wave introduced: scriptcheck.js's corrected comment cited 2 <strong> excerpts against the 104-excerpt sentence when 2 was the single-room figure and 5 is the right one, and the new test carried a dead binding. Results measured on both surfaces: 0 of 104 rail excerpts and 0 of 12 drawer clips carry markup, median 1462 to 244 characters, the Walkman card 1730px to 764px, and 0 of 9 cards need scrolling where 9 of 9 did.

waves.name: the-answer-outranks-the-gloss
waves.rationale: The highest-ranked row in the register, blocked for two waves on one builder decision: is the answer the note, or the source quotation? Answered 2026-08-11 as the source quotation, which made it a frontend wave with no contract risk. Wave 4 is what made that answer available — before it, a no-note card fell back to 2900 characters of raw markdown.
waves.closeOut: Built and closed the same day. The row's second 'hole to close first' was a misreading rather than a hole: the verifier prompt makes the note optional on confirmed and anachronism, so a card without one is the designed common case (4 of 9 real claims), and the card had been built as though the note were the answer. Citation block is now a median 62.2% of the card where the note was 1.2%. The quantifier trap on 'the sources below' was checked against verdicts.py:275-277 rather than assumed, and the test pins the server's guarded tuple to the card's promising slugs.

waves.name: the-room-after-it-files
waves.rationale: The three highest-ranked rows left (12, 12, 9) and all three live on one surface: the room a writer opens after a build files. The drawer they click sends itself off screen, the number on the docket says the ledger vouched for searches it only counted as issued, and the drawer's own hanging-folder construction has 1.6px of tuck where it needs about 9. Every figure in the brief was re-measured 2026-08-11 rather than carried from the audit.
waves.closeOut: ran 2026-08-11. Three items, three commits. F-007's fix direction changed twice under measurement (scroll the card not the toggle; click handler not setOpen) and needed a scroll-margin-top no row anticipated. The brief's open question — should closing scroll — was answered by measuring: no, the browser's scroll anchoring already compensates. F-011's clip-path re-slope was necessary and is quantified. The grid's 'cannot drift' claim was verified rather than trusted: card tops identical before and after. Two of the wave's own tests were wrong first and caught by mutation rather than review.

waves.name: said-twice-meant-once
waves.rationale: Six rows, one shape: a value declared more than once and drifting. Two of them (F-017, F-019) render byte-identical pixels, which is why wave 3 passed on them — so the wave's argument is F-016, where the same duplication has ALREADY drifted far enough to be visible as an 8px left-edge break between two stacked cards in 10-bible. Ship the visible defect and close the two that would become it. F-018 goes first because it corrects the measuring stick every other wave is judged against.
